questions.question: Find the greatest number that will divide 57, 93 and 191 so as to leave the same remainder in each case.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Numbers: 57, 93, 191

**Concept:**

The greatest number that leaves the same remainder when dividing multiple numbers is the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the differences between those numbers.

**Calculation:**

Find the differences between the numbers ⇒ 93 - 57 = 36, 191 - 93 = 98

The GCD of 36 and 98 is 2

**Therefore, the greatest number that will divide 57, 93 and 191 so as to leave the same remainder in each case is 2.**

questions.question: If radius of a hemisphere = radius of a cone = height of the cone, then what will be the ratio of the curved surfaces area of this hemisphere and curved surface area of this cone?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Radius of Hemisphere = Radius of Cone = Height of Cone

**Formula Used:**

**1.** Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere = 2πr² 

**2.** Curved Surface Area of Cone = πrl

Where l = Slant Height

**Calculation:**

For cone,

Slant height = l = √{r²+h²}

⇒ l = √{r²+r²} = (√2)r ----[Radius of Cone = Height of Cone]

Curved Surface Area of Cone = πr[(√2)r]

Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere = 2πr2

CSA of Hemisphere : CSA of Cone = 2πr2 : πr[(√2)r]

⇒ CSA of Hemisphere : CSA of Cone = √2 : 1

**∴ The ratio of the curved surface area of the hemisphere to the curved surface area of the cone is √2 ∶ 1.**

questions.question: A dealer announces 8% and 18% discounts on a watch. If the selling price of the watch is ₹943, then the marked price of the watch is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Selling price = ₹943

Discounts = 8%, 18%

**Concept:**

The effective selling price after consecutive discounts of x% and y% on the marked price is (100 - x)(100 - y)% of the marked price.

**Calculation:**

Let the marked price be 'M'

⇒ 0.82 × 0.92 × M = 943

⇒ M = 943/(0.82 × 0.92)

**Therefore, the marked price of the watch is ₹1,250.**

questions.question: A merchant bought 1200 items for ₹1,800 and he sold them at the rate of 1000 for ₹1,600. Calculate gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Cost Price for 1200 items = ₹1,800

Selling Price for 1000 items = ₹1,600

**Concept:**

The percentage profit/loss is ((Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price) × 100%.

**Calculation:**

Cost Price for 1 item = 1800/1200 = ₹1.5

Selling Price for 1 item = 1600/1000 = ₹1.6

Profit percentage = ((1.6 - 1.5)/1.5) × 100% = 20/3%

**Therefore, the gain percentage is 20/3%.**

questions.question: A dealer sells wheat at 25% profit and uses a weight 5% less than the actual measure. His gain percentage is:

Profit = 25%

False weight = 5% less

**Concept:**

If a dealer uses less weight than actual, the effective profit is (100 + profit%)/(100 - false weight%) × 100

**Calculation:**

Effective profit = (125/95) × 100 = 31(11)/(19) \%

**Therefore, the dealer's effective gain percentage is 31(11)/(19) \%**

questions.question: The fourth proportional of the numbers 0.002, 0.04 and 0.0006 is ______.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Numbers: 0.002, 0.04, 0.0006

**Concept:**

The fourth proportional of three numbers a, b, c is given by (b × c)/a.

**Calculation:**

Fourth proportional = (0.04 × 0.0006)/0.002

**Therefore, the fourth proportional of the numbers 0.002, 0.04 and 0.0006 is 1.2 × 10⁻².**

questions.question: P, Q, and R can do a piece of work in 38 days. Q and R can do the work in 76 days. Find the number of days in which P can complete the same work.
questions.solution:
**Given**

P, Q, R can complete the work in 38 days.

Q and R can complete the work in 76 days.

**Concept:**

If A and B together can complete a job in 'd' days and B alone can complete the same job in 'f' days, then A alone can complete the job in (d × f) / (f - d) days.

**Calculation:**

Time taken by P alone to complete the work = (38 × 76)/(76 - 38)

**Hence, P alone can complete the work in 76 days.**

questions.question: R goes to the post office from home covering a distance of 5 km and 400 metres in half an hour, and then goes to office covering a distance of 25 km and 750 metres in 90 minutes. What is his average speed from home to office in km/h?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Distance covered from home to post office = 5 km + 400 m = 5.4 km

Time taken = 0.5 hour

Distance covered from post office to office = 25 km + 750 m = 25.75 km

Time taken = 1.5 hours

**Concept:**

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

**Calculation:**

Total distance = 5.4 km + 25.75 km = 31.15 km

Total time = 0.5 hr + 1.5 hr = 2 hr

Average speed = 31.15 km/2 hr

**Therefore, the average speed from home to office is 15.575 km/h.**

questions.question: If the average of p, q and r is A and pq + qr + rp = 0, then the value of (p² + q ² + r²)/(27) is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Average of p, q and r = A

pq + qr + rp = 0

**Concept:**

Average = sum of all number/total numbers.

**Calculation:**

p + q + r = 3A (given)

Square both sides:

⇒ p² + q² + r² + 2(pq + qr + rp) = 9A²

⇒ p2 + q2 + r2 = 9A2

⇒ ((p² + q² + r²))/(27) = (9A²)/(27) 

⇒ A²/3

**Therefore, the value of ((p² + q² + r²))/(27) is A²/3.**

questions.question: If 'x' is divisible by 3 and 2, then 2x³ + 3x² is divisible by :
questions.solution:
**Given**

'x' is divisible by 2 and 3

**Calculation:**

If x is divisible by 3, 2 then LCM is 6.

The expression is 2x³ + 3x² = 2 × 216 + 3 × 36 = 412 + 108 = 540

As 540 is divisible by 108, 2x3 + 3x2 is divisible by 108.

**Therefore, 2x³ + 3x² is divisible by 108.**

questions.question: The discount on a toy is 15%. A successive discount of 15% is also offered. What is the effective discount on the toy
questions.solution:
**Given**

Initial discount = 15%

Successive discount = 15%

**Concept:**

The net discount percentage on successive discounts of x% and y% is given by x + y - xy/100%.

**Calculation:**

Net discount = 15 + 15 - (15 × 15)/100 = 27.75%

**Therefore, the effective discount on the toy is 27.75%.**

questions.question: In an election between two contestants, 25% of the total votes are marked as invalid due to technical problem. The winner gets 7500 votes, which are (2)/(3) of the total valid votes. The difference in votes of the winner and invalid votes is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Invalid votes = 25% of total votes

Winner's votes = 2/3 of total valid votes

**Concept:**

The number of valid votes is (1 - invalid votes %) of total votes.

**Calculation:**

Let the total votes are 100x.

25% invalid, so remaining are 75x

According to question

 75x × 2/3 = 7500

x = 150

Total invalid votes = 25 × 150 = 3750

The difference in votes of the winner and invalid votes is = 7500 - 3750 = 3750.

**Therefore, the difference in votes of the winner and invalid votes is 3750.**

questions.question: A square and an equilateral triangle have equal perimeters. If the diagonal of the square is 12sqrt{2} cm, then the area of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Perimeter of square = Perimeter of equilateral triangle

Diagonal of square = 12√2 cm

**Concept:**

The side of a square given its diagonal is d/√2 and the area of an equilateral triangle given its side is (s²√3)/4.

**Calculation:**

Side of square = 12√2/√2 = 12 cm

Perimeter of triangle = Perimeter of square

3a = 12 × 4

a = 16

Area of equilateral triangle = (16²√3)/4

**Therefore, the area of the triangle is 64√3 cm².**

questions.question: At what rate of compound interest per annum, compounding annually, does a sum of money become (625)/(256) times itself in 4 years?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Final amount = (625)/(256) times the initial amount

Time = 4 years

**Concept:**

The rate of compound interest is found from the formula A = P(1 + r/n)⁽ⁿt⁾, where A is the final amount, P is the initial amount, r is the annual interest rate, n is the number of times the interest is compounded per year, and t is the time in years.

**Calculation:**

(625)/(256) = (1 + r)⁴

Take the fourth root of both sides to solve for r

**Therefore, the rate of compound interest is 0.25 or 25% per annum.**

questions.question: A board 100 cm long is trimmed to 86 cm. What percentage has been removed?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Original length of the board = 100 cm

Trimmed length of the board = 86 cm

**Concept:**

The percentage removed is calculated as ((Original length - Trimmed length)/Original length) × 100%.

**Calculation:**

Percentage removed = ((100 - 86)/100) × 100%

**Therefore, 14% of the board has been removed.**

questions.question: Find the average of the numbers 517, 139, 195, 176 and 192.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Numbers: 517, 139, 195, 176, 192

**Concept:**

The average of a set of numbers is the sum of the numbers divided by the count of numbers.

**Calculation:**

Average = (517 + 139 + 195 + 176 + 192)/5

**Therefore, the average of the numbers 517, 139, 195, 176 and 192 is 243.8.**

questions.question: Rohan and Sohan can complete a piece of work in 10 days and 12 days, respectively. If they work on alternate days, starting with Sohan, in how many days will the whole work be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Rohan can complete a piece of work in 10 days.

Sohan can complete the same work in 12 days.

**Calculation:**

LCM of 10 and 12 is 60.

Efficiency of Rohan = 60/10 = 6

Efficiency of sohan = 60/12 = 5

so, 2 days work will be 11 units.

10 days work will be 55 units.

Now, Sohan will work on 11th day. so 10 + 1 = 11 days

**Hence, the work will be completed in 11 days.**

questions.question: A runs at a speed that is (11)/(9) times the speed of B. If B is allowed to have a head start such that B beats A by (1)/(3) of the length of the race, what part of the length of the race has been given as head start to B over A? [Note: Consider A and B to start running at the same time.]
questions.solution:
**Given**

A's speed = 11/9 times B's speed

B beats A by 1/3 of the length of the race

**Calculation:**

The ratio of speed of A and B is 11 : 9

Let the total race be 90 units.

Let the head start given by B to A is x.

Total distance covered by A = 60 units which is 1/3 less of total distance.

Total distance covered by B = 90 - x

According to the question:

⇒ 60/11 = (90 - x)/9

⇒ 11x = 450

⇒ x = 450/11

The part is = 450/(11 × 90) = 5/11

**Therefore, the part of the length of the race that has been given as a head start to B over A is 5/11.**

questions.question: The price of a jacket and handbag are in the ratio of 3 : 2. If a jacket costs ₹600 more than the handbag, then the price of the handbag is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Price ratio of jacket to handbag = 3 ∶ 2

Jacket costs ₹600 more than the handbag

**Concept:**

If the price ratio of two items is 'a ∶ b' and the difference in their costs is 'd', then the cost of the cheaper item is 'd × b/(a - b)'.

**Calculation:**

Cost of handbag = 600 × 2/(3 - 2)

**Therefore, the price of the handbag is ₹1,200.**
